text:
Lina (Support): Heads-up — GreenWave (acct GW-2119) reports being charged twice for their annual renewal. Two invoices in our system: INV-2026-03-08-001 (auto-renew) and INV-2026-03-08-002 (manual retry). Both show as paid. Amount: €12,500. PO# GW-PO-987 is attached to the account. Customer is in Germany and provided VAT ID DE123456789 — they say this should be reverse-charged (0% VAT). Customer requests one charge reversed and a credit note for the duplicate invoice. Ticket created: SUP-3821. Repro note: payments webhook was retried after a 500 from our endpoint; logs attached.

James (Billing): Thanks Lina. Can you confirm which transaction was captured first? Also do we refund to card or issue a credit note / void invoice? Customer said refund to card preferred but we need finance sign-off for VAT handling.

Lina (Support): Both charges are marked "succeeded" / captured in the PSP. Transactions: ch_1J9abcXYZ (12:01 UTC) and ch_1J9abcXYY (12:03 UTC). Payment intents: pi_ABC123 and pi_DEF456. Duplicate invoice is INV-2026-03-08-002. Customer confirms refund to card is fine. They attached the EU VAT certificate.

Maya (Finance): We can refund; processor timeline is typically 2–5 business days for funds to appear. For bookkeeping we usually issue a credit note against the duplicate invoice and process the refund in the PSP so our ledger shows both the credit note and the refund. I need GL code 4-4320 and cost center — please confirm. Also need explicit customer confirmation that refund is acceptable (Lina, can you confirm in the ticket?).

Raj (Payments Eng): I checked the payments/webhook logs. Root cause: event evt_zz_retry hit our webhook at 12:02; our endpoint returned 500 for the first delivery and our retry created a second charge because idempotency key wasn't applied to the internal charge creation path. Short SQL to find duplicates:

```
-- find duplicate captured charges for this account
SELECT id, payment_intent, processor_charge_id, status, created_at
FROM payments
WHERE account_id = 'GW-2119' AND amount_cents = 1250000
ORDER BY created_at;
```

I can run a one-off to mark the earlier event as processed and block the duplicate, but I recommend refunding the second charge to keep a clean audit trail. I'll also open PR to enforce idempotency for webhook-replayed events (PR #987).

James (Billing): Fine with refund + credit note. Lina, please get customer OK in the ticket and share the exact processor charge id we should refund.

Lina (Support): Customer replied in ticket and approved refund to card. They asked we zero-rate VAT (reverse-charge). Confirming refund target: ch_1J9abcXYY (the later charge). Marking SUP-3821 as "awaiting finance action".

Ops Bot: Refund initiated: refund_2026_GW_001 for processor charge ch_1J9abcXYY — status: pending.

Maya (Finance): Refund initiated in PSP and credit note created: CN-2026-004 against INV-2026-03-08-002. Invoice INV-2026-03-08-002 will be voided in accounting after refund clears. Posting GL: 4-4320, Cost center: RND. ETA: accounting entries posted today; customer emailed copy of credit note and refund receipt.

Raj (Payments Eng): I've deployed a temporary rate-limit and fixed the idempotency check for webhook retries on the staging branch; will promote to prod after a quick smoke test. Logged the incident and linked to SUP-3821.

Lina (Support): Customer confirmed they received the credit note and saw the refund pending in their bank. They'll allow ticket to be closed once refund posts. Closing actions: finance to reconcile when refund clears; payments eng to ship idempotency fix. SUP-3821 -> will be resolved after final reconciliation. :white_check_mark:
